connectors.dingtalk: Work with DingTalk documents, calendars, tasks and more using its official CLI. This connector is intended for DingTalk’s public cloud edition; the dedicated edition has not been tested. Some organizations’ security policies may prevent authorization.
connectors.feishu: Work with Feishu documents, messages, calendars and tasks through the official CLI.
connectors.wecom: Scan to bind a WeCom bot and use the capabilities enabled by your organization.

addc.title: Add connector
addc.sub: A connector is an MCP server that gives finx more tools. Paste its address or the command that starts it; finx checks the rest.
addc.name: Name
addc.nameNote: Shown in the list, and the prefix of its tools' names.
addc.nameNoteSuggested: Shown in the connector list and used as its tools' prefix. Press Tab to fill in {{name}}, or leave it empty to use it.
addc.badName: Letters, digits, - and _ only, at most 32 characters
addc.taken: There is a connector named {{name}} already; choose another name

bad.empty: Enter an address or a command
bad.json: This looks like JSON, but it does not parse
bad.jsonServer: No server in the JSON (it needs command or url)
bad.scheme: A remote address starts with http:// or https://

addc.willCheck: finx checks whether it needs a sign-in first
addc.insecure: not https: a token would travel in clear text

note.apiKey: No sign-in settings published; it probably takes an API key

addc.oauthDesc: Sign in with your {{issuer}} account in the browser; the token is kept in the system keychain and renewed when it expires.
addc.ownDesc: An app you registered with the provider, for example when your company requires a fixed client ID.
addc.redirect: When registering the app with {{issuer}}, set the callback address to
addc.tokenDesc: Puts the token the provider gave you in a request header. For servers that take an API key instead of OAuth.
addc.tokenPlaceholder: Paste the token; it goes to the keychain
addc.tokenRefused: The server refused this token (HTTP 401). Check that it is right and allowed.
addc.noneDesc: The server is open; finx connects directly.
addc.httpDesc: The current MCP transport. Use it unless the server only supports SSE.
addc.sseDesc: The older transport being phased out. Chosen when the address ends in /sse.
addc.trust: Only add connectors from developers you trust. Which tools a connector offers and what they return is up to its developer; finx cannot verify it or promise it will not change.
addc.download: The first run of {{program}} downloads first; the check may take a while.
addc.localTrust: A local command runs as you on this computer and can read and write what you can. Only add commands you trust.
addc.loginTitle: Sign in to {{name}} in your browser
addc.loginText: The sign-in page of {{issuer}} is open in your browser. After you sign in and allow access, you come back here.

found.open: Checked: the server accepted the connection; no authentication needed.
found.oauth: Checked: the server asks you to sign in; its sign-in service is {{issuer}}.
found.oauthOwn: Checked: the server asks you to sign in, but {{issuer}} does not let apps register on their own, so it needs your own OAuth app.
found.token: Checked: the server needs authentication but publishes no sign-in service; it most likely wants a token or API key.
found.unreached: Checked: the address didn't answer this time; below are the saved settings.

what.token: The token is kept in the system keychain; the config file holds only a reference.
what.tokenEnv: The token is kept in the system keychain and given to the command as {{env}}.

addc.patHint: If the provider also offers personal access tokens, choosing "Token or API key" is simpler.
addc.envNote: Variables whose names look like secrets are locked: their values go to the system keychain and the config file holds only a reference. Click the lock to switch.
addc.clientAutoDesc: finx registers itself with the sign-in service; nothing to set up.
addc.clientAutoOff: {{issuer}} does not let apps register on their own
addc.duplicate: {{name}} already reaches this service; one connector per service is enough.
addc.saved: Saved in the keychain · type a new value to replace it

hints.dingtalk: Sign in and authorize on DingTalk’s official page. This connector is intended for DingTalk’s public cloud edition; the dedicated edition has not been tested. Some organizations’ security policies may prevent authorization; contact your administrator to confirm access. You can sign out or disable the connector at any time.
hints.feishu: First create a dedicated app on Feishu, then complete user consent in the next browser page. The connector enables only after both steps and a connection check. Your organization may require admin approval.
hints.wecom: Scan the official WeCom page to bind a bot. Your organization controls available capabilities. Signing out clears local credentials; manage the server-side binding in WeCom.

managed.partialPermissions: Connected with partial permissions. Authorized features are available; other features require additional consent or approval from your organization.
